messages:
olivia (People Ops): Mark asked a nuanced question: he's going on an unpaid parental leave but expects to do a few "gig" stipend payments sporadically that will run through payroll. He wants to know how those intermittent pays interact with our 401(k) auto-escalation, employer match, and HSA employer contribution proration. Any quick guidance for him?

sanjay (Payroll): Short: payroll treats each pay as independent. If a stipend is run through payroll and it's taxable wages, we'll apply active election percentages that are in effect for that employee at that pay. If the vendor has updated the election while you're on leave, that new % will apply to any pay that has deductions.

helen (Benefits): Important nuance: our plan's auto-escalation is vendor-driven and can be suspended per participant. If auto-escalation runs while the employee is off but elections are updated in the vendor system, any subsequent stipend pay that has withholding will use the new percentage. If the employee wants to avoid that, we should pause escalation or put a payroll hold for stipend runs.

mark (IC): I absolutely don't want a surprise 5% deferral hitting a small stipend. How do I prevent it? Can Benefits pause escalation for me only for the leave period?

plan-bot: Ticket CREATED: VND-PAUSE-221  "participant escalation pause request". Expected vendor response 2 business days.

helen (Benefits): Yes we can pause escalation for individual participants via vendor form (e-sign usually). Steps: 1) Employee emails benefits@ with leave start/end and request to pause auto-escalation. 2) Benefits files the vendor pause form. 3) Payroll watches vendor feed for an "escalation_suspended" flag before processing any ad-hoc stipend pay.

sanjay (Payroll): Operationally, I'll add a pre-check: any ad-hoc stipend payroll run will consult the vendor feed for that employee. If we see escalation_suspended then we won't apply any vendor-driven election changes to that pay. If the vendor doesn't provide the flag in time, payroll can apply a manual election override for that pay if Benefits asks.

olivia (People Ops): That sounds like three possible ways to avoid changes: 1) pause escalation at the vendor, 2) payroll manual override on stipend pays, 3) employee temporarily set election to preferred % before stipend. Which do we recommend?

helen (Benefits): Recommended order: 1) Pause escalation (preferred) so system state matches employee intent. 2) If pause can't be processed before stipend, request payroll override for the specific pay. 3) Avoid employees manually lowering elections because that may be permanent unless they remember to revert.

mark (IC): OK. What about employer match and HSA employer contribution rules if I only have a few stipend pays while on leave? Will I get pro-rated HSA employer contribution? And match?

helen (Benefits): Match: employer match is calculated on actual contributions per pay period. If a stipend pay has employee deferrals, match will apply to that pay up to plan limits. If you have no deferrals on a pay, no match for that pay. HSA employer contributions: we prorate the annual employer HSA seed based on eligible pay periods where we consider the employee "eligible" (e.g., benefits-eligible status). If you're on unpaid leave and considered ineligible for certain plan-year employer HSA credits, you may get a prorated amount. Small stipend pays that are taxable and processed via payroll typically don't change your eligibility classification unless they qualify as eligible pay periods per policy. We'll calculate exact proration if needed.

sanjay (Payroll): Practically, if you have a 1-off stipend that gets run through payroll and it's classified as eligible compensation for benefits, you'll receive any per-pay employer HSA contribution tied to that pay (if our process treats it that way). But global proration for the plan year is separate and will be reconciled at year-end; you might see a small additional employer HSA deposit or an adjustment depending on our proration logic.

olivia (People Ops): Action items: 1) Mark to email benefits@redwood.com with leave dates and request pause if he wants escalation paused. 2) Sanjay to add payroll pre-check for stipend runs for escalation_suspended flag and to be ready to apply manual override. 3) Helen to prepare a 2-line FAQ for handbook clarifying stipend + auto-escalation interaction and HSA proration note.

mark (IC): I'll send the pause request now. Quick Q: will pausing escalation change my scheduled escalation cycle after I return? Will it pick up where it left off or restart?

helen (Benefits): Vendor behavior varies. Some vendors resume escalation where it left off (i.e., next scheduled bump increments from previous %) while others treat pause as skipping a cycle. When we submit a pause we confirm with vendor whether they will resume automatically on a given return date or if the participant needs to request resume. We'll document the vendor response in the ticket and include it in the reply to you.

plan-bot: VND-PAUSE-221 updated: vendor confirms e-sign pause available, will include escalation_suspended flag and offers an optional resume-on-date parameter. Processing ETA: 1 payroll cycle after signature.

olivia (People Ops): Thanks all. Helen  please draft that FAQ and include language: "If you take unpaid leave and expect ad-hoc stipend pays, contact Benefits to pause auto-escalation or request Payroll override. Match applies only to actual contributions; HSA employer contributions are prorated by eligible pay periods and may be adjusted after migration/year-end." We'll post in #benefits-updates once VND-PAUSE-221 is closed.

mark (IC): Sent the email to benefits@ with my dates and requested pause. Thanks everyone for the clear steps. :thumbsup:
